title: Conditions of the Master Grain Marketing Agreement: The Share of a Shortfall the Cooperative Retains
content:
The retained share of the shortfall on a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts is the part of the bushels the member has not delivered that the cooperative has already sold on and will not release by amendment; the rest of the shortfall comes off the contract.

**Clause 1.** Where the tickets credit at least half the bushels the contract commits and four or more tickets stand against it, the retained share is 0.4 of the shortfall.

**Clause 2.** Where tickets stand against the contract but that pair of conditions is not met, the retained share is 0.65 of the shortfall.

**Clause 3.** Where no ticket stands against the contract, the whole of the shortfall is retained and the amendment releases nothing.

## The clauses in combination

| Tickets standing | Bushels the tickets credit, against the bushels committed | Retained share |
|---|---|---|
| 4 or more | at least half | 0.4 |
| 4 or more | less than half | 0.65 |
| 1 to 3 | either way | 0.65 |
| none | — | the whole of it |

Half the committed bushels is itself enough to satisfy the first clause, and four tickets is itself enough; three tickets crediting nine tenths of the commitment falls to the second clause, and so do five tickets crediting a third of it.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

On a contract committing 20,000 bushels whose five tickets credit 12,000, the shortfall is 8,000 bushels and the retained share is 0.4 of it, being 3,200 bushels. Where only two tickets stand, crediting the same 12,000 bushels, the retained share is 0.65 of the 8,000, being 5,200 bushels. Where no ticket stands at all, the whole 20,000 bushel shortfall is retained.
